title: Meet China’s AI Enforcers - The Wire China
gist: Beijing has gone all-in on AI for technological self-sufficiency but is grappling with how to regulate it, extending its decades-old content-control approach, starting with 2017-2018 rules on deepfakes and public-opinion sway. Only the teaser is available (paywalled).

insights.claim: Beijing has gone all-in on AI as a pathway to technological self-sufficiency, but with limits on how the industry may develop.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Chinese AI policy is both an industrial push and a control regime; expect regulation to shape domestic AI products.
insights.quote: Beijing has gone all-in on AI as a pathway to technological self-sufficiency, but with limits

insights.claim: China's initial AI regulation in 2017 and 2018 followed its long-standing content-management model, focusing on deepfakes and AI's potential to sway public opinion.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Chinese AI rules originate in information-control priorities, which shapes compliance burdens for AI firms.
